answer: Non-kin attestation finality resists sybils: an identity reaches finality only when K attesters vouch for it who share no common invite-ancestor — no kin edge — so a cluster grown from one inviter forms a kin-clique that cannot certify its own members. A shale-layered farm of a thousand heads off a single beacon-invite is one island in the graph: its internal edges are all kin, worthless for finality, and it must still source K genuinely independent honest attesters per identity. Headcount inside the clique buys no finality; only real external non-kin edges do, and those are scarce.
